scope.method: Read-only manuscript text/diffs and research-log correction chain. Raw experiment output was not rehashed or decoded; cards describe manuscript assertions unless explicitly qualified.

cards.researchquestion: Did the manuscript establish a low-rate, perceptually acceptable hybrid codec with a no-worse fallback?
cards.observation: No. The May abstract asserted about 60 VMAF below 200 kbps and 7–10× lower bandwidth. The introduction promised fallback safety. The problem section reported about 60% size reduction after object/background separation and another 36% after pose-cGAN synthesis, while omitting VMAF and assuming generated appearance acceptable. A row says 230 KB and 294 MB against 950 KB and 1.2 MB and an overall 4.55 MB to 2.92 MB; units conflict. Archived reviewers point to narrow tennis scope, missing modern/learned baselines, no visual or temporal validation, speed, and generality.
cards.limitations: These are manuscript assertions, not experiment verification; one short 4K/50 fps clip description, no calibrated generated quality, incomplete payload accounting, and unresolved MB/KB conflict. Reviews are context only.
cards.latercorrections: 0603f65 removes the inherited abstract claim; the July full-match log says fallback was selected on every observed sub-chunk; 6f86e3b later reports a scoped paired rate loss.
cards.paperuse: If history matters, say early claims were withdrawn after evidence and instrumentation audits. Do not repeat the old VMAF, bandwidth, size-reduction, or never-worse claims as results.

cards.stage: July generator probes and evaluator repair
cards.researchquestion: Do early generator scores rank candidate engines for PointStream?
cards.observation: No. G2 reported Pix2Pix PSNR 22.98/VMAF 15.79, SPADE 21.89/3.00, and pose-ControlNet 9.76/0.11, but no rung completed; the campaign ended through TypeError, CUDA OOM, interruption and out-of-order rows. A condition/decoder mismatch affected evaluation, and relevant training data had 33% wrong pairs and 23% missing pairs. Fixed-path remeasurement on 12 probes moved ControlNet to 16.06 dB (+6.3 dB) and Pix2Pix down to 15.39 dB. Crop VMAF remained near zero and unusable for ranking. Old LPIPS was uncalibrated VGG distance (.083 unrelated vs .085 good); reversed libvmaf inputs made blur score 100 vs 97.4 identical. Separately, coded_roundtrip re-encoded reconstructions through default libx264 through 27 August.
cards.limitations: Corrected scores remain diagnostic: low crop quality, bad pairing, no source-level generator win, and crop VMAF saturation. Scorer, dataset and delivered-output defects are separate.
cards.latercorrections: 5c3a5b3 voids pre-23-August LPIPS/VMAF. 6f86e3b flags coded_roundtrip qualities before 28 August as suspect due to lossy re-encode.
cards.paperuse: Describe early rankings as retracted. Replacement evidence must identify exact pairing, checkpoint, invocation, region, resolution-calibrated metric and static-copy control.

cards.researchquestion: Which combinations define PointStream, and what would count as a component benefit?
cards.observation: The paper formalizes appearance, motion, temporal policy, background and residual coordinates. A valid lattice point must pair with a generator that consumes the chosen appearance/motion input. Component value is intended to use swept rate–distortion curves against the all-off conventional-video corner. Construction checks cover buildable corners, all-off source behavior, disabled-detector cost, and residual absent/lossless payload changes. The paper explicitly says no end-to-end lattice sweep or quantitative component ablation exists. AVC addroi at fixed QP yielded identical 7,627-byte streams and 0.00 dB ROI movement; AV1 matched-QP ROI used 3.08% more bytes for +0.35 dB inside and 0.00 outside, so equal-rate benefit is unknown.
cards.limitations: Construction tests establish contracts, not rate or quality benefit. ROI depends on actual encoder/version: HEVC remained unverified, and the surveyed VVC build had no caller-controlled region map. No fair region-controlled ladder was run.
cards.latercorrections: 6f86e3b retains no-goal/hole markers for the lattice and reports no region-controlled ladder.
cards.paperuse: Call this a design/evaluation lattice. Separate construction tests from codec outcomes and state that ablation and matched-rate ROI results are outstanding.

cards.researchquestion: How much changed-target coding headroom appears when players are removed or panorama replaces inter-coded background?
cards.observation: A synthetic 96×128/16-frame/3-seed probe reported 12.2% foreground BD-rate saving and a 17.4× panorama/JPEG ratio, then was replaced because player area and still-image baseline did not represent 4K broadcasts. The first real two-window/48-frame 4K probe reported 15.2–26.0% foreground and 34.4–68.9% background savings; it was directional at n=2 and had a VVC QP/integration confound. The expanded study reports eight 48-frame windows from six matches at 3840×2160/24 fps. Player area is 1.11±0.32%; foreground means are AVC 17.0±3.1%, HEVC 18.3±3.4%, AV1 15.4±2.8%, VVC 14.2±2.6%; background means are AVC 64.3±8.4% (n=6), HEVC 66.5±7.3% (n=7), AV1 78.0±5.6% (n=8), VVC 76.1±3.9% (n=8). AVC bitrate concentration is 18.9±5.0× (per-clip savings/player area). Two AVC scenes are low at 1.1% and 9.9% savings.
cards.limitations: Changed-target conventional-codec diagnostic, not PointStream. Background BD-rate excludes windows without adequate overlap. An early VVC QP mismatch confounded the apparent gap; raw experiment outputs were not recertified in this extraction.
cards.latercorrections: f32c1cf widens to n=8 and withdraws the VVC-generation trend: paired AVC–VVC deltas +0.028±0.015 at common QP and +0.023±0.017 on a common PSNR slice. Final tables expose per-window values and exclusions.
cards.paperuse: Across eligible 4K tennis windows, player removal changed conventional-codec BD-rate by a mean 14.2–18.3% while silhouettes covered 1.11±0.32% of frame area. Label this as changed-target headroom, with valid n and overlap exclusions.

cards.researchquestion: Do metrics order known-quality anchors correctly, and can scores transfer across crop sizes?
cards.observation: On native 4K, LPIPS AlexNet calibration is 0 identical, .0171 mild blur, .2982 severe blur, .5493 unrelated. At 960×540 severe blur is .613 versus .522 unrelated. VMAF on two tested frames has a 97.54 identical-pair ceiling and 0 severe-blur/unrelated floor. VMAF is frame-level; LPIPS carries region-scoped scoring. Earlier VGG-as-LPIPS had .083/.085 unrelated/good separation and reversed libvmaf inputs scored blur 100 vs identical 97.4.
cards.limitations: Two-frame/content-specific calibration is not universal. Resolution changes LPIPS ordering; crop VMAF is unsuitable under noted libvmaf size/content constraints. Coded-roundtrip output contamination is separate from metric correctness.
cards.latercorrections: All pre-23-August perceptual values are void; all pre-28-August coded_roundtrip qualities are flagged suspect.
cards.paperuse: Report metric, region and resolution together. Do not compare across resolution as if calibration transfers or cite calibration anchors as generator-quality evidence.

cards.stage: generator-baseline table and unresolved prose mismatch
cards.researchquestion: Did tested generators outperform static copy on reported probe metrics?
cards.observation: Prose/comments say static copy beats every generator on PSNR and LPIPS. Table contradicts the PSNR half: static copy 11.82 dB; Pose-ControlNet 12.03; Segmentation-ControlNet 12.19; AA clip 11.57. No PSNR error bars are supplied. LPIPS table values favor static copy (.451±.022) over pose .603±.024, segmentation .560±.021, AA .569±.021. A NOTE instead compares AA .570 against a “static copy at the same offset” .582, slightly favoring AA for that pair, while the table calls .451 the floor. Protocol reconciliation is absent.
cards.limitations: 12 probe clips; exact mask/offset protocol unresolved; AA fine-tuning saw all seven tennis videos, including later held-out videos, so in-domain only. LPIPS probe does not establish unseen-match generalization. IP-Adapter remained not citable.
cards.latercorrections: No later correction through 29 August resolves the PSNR or same-offset LPIPS mismatch.
cards.paperuse: Do not claim every generator loses on both metrics. At most report table LPIPS probe values after resolving the two static-copy definitions; make AA in-domain-only explicit.

cards.stage: paired ladder and residual curve, 29 August
cards.researchquestion: Does the measured PointStream configuration beat codec ladders, and what sets its cost?
cards.observation: On the most static 8-frame 4K Alcaraz window, luma-PSNR BD-rate penalties are +116.8% vs AV1 over 39.45–44.02 dB, +166.8% HEVC, +165.9% AVC, +378.1% VVC. On a dynamic window, PointStream reaches 31.0 dB while AV1 lowest rung is 38.03 dB, so curves do not overlap. Generation is disabled. JPEG plate is 88–91% of payload; residual 3–9%. Plate+crops without residual is 487,643 B/35.37 dB vs AV1 85,995 B/39.45 dB. Static residual curve: absent 487,643 B/35.37, coarse 491,977/40.77, medium 508,413/43.33, fine 812,971/46.11; lossless array 398,618,843 B excluded. One-plate probe near 38 dB: JPEG 283,431 B, AV1 intra 79,726 B, VVC intra 68,477 B. Panorama interframe note reports 31–53% AV1 saving between points but marks the feature unimplemented.
cards.limitations: Eight frames/two windows; one preset per codec with encoder effort unmatched across codecs; BD-rate only over overlap; no ROI ladder, encode-time axis, or generator. Residual sweep bundles knobs and covers one codec/two clips. Still-image codec and panorama delta are not integrated; delta study did not enforce low-delay/no-B-frame/no-lookahead conditions.
cards.latercorrections: No later correction through the extraction window. Paper says no system win and leaves rate/time/ROI/corpus gaps.
cards.paperuse: Report a scoped negative for the exact generator-disabled eight-frame implementation. Explain plate dominance and local residual behavior; do not infer a benefit from unswept still coding or unimplemented panorama delta.

cards.stage: cross-section status contradictions in final August snapshot
cards.researchquestion: Do section status statements consistently distinguish completed studies from future work and open evaluation holes?
cards.observation: No. Future Work says two domain profiles are evaluated, while Evaluation says generalization was not run in either domain. Future Work says schema richness is measured using progressively sparser skeleton renderings, while Evaluation says the object-representation comparison was not run and the end-to-end lattice sweep is absent. No claim marker or artifact reference reconciles these statements.
cards.limitations: This extraction checked manuscript text and markers, not implementation outputs; it cannot determine whether a separate artifact existed. The text itself is internally inconsistent.
cards.latercorrections: No correction appears in the inspected history through 29 August.
cards.paperuse: Use past tense only for studies backed by a separately identified claim/artifact. Otherwise rewrite these statements as proposed measurements and retain the evaluation holes.
